links.comparator_used: Blinded radiologist (board-certified radiologist and radiology resident) pairwise evaluation of the same report pairs
links.outcome: Agreement of LLM judges with radiologist ratings on translation quality (terminology accuracy, readability, overall quality, radiologist-style authenticity)
links.effect: Radiologist-LLM judge agreement QWK=-0.04 to 0.15 (near zero); the two radiologists also agreed poorly (QWK=0.01 to 0.06). All 3 LLM judges favored the LLM translation on all criteria (70%-99%) and rated it more radiologist-like in >93% of cases.
links.tradeoff: LLM judges showed a strong preference for LLM-generated output and negligible agreement with radiologists, so automated evaluation alone was insufficient. The two radiologists also differed substantially from each other.
links.quote: Agreement between radiologists and LLM judges was near zero (QWK=-0.04 to 0.15).

links.comparator_used: Human-edited Japanese translation of the same chest CT reports
links.outcome: Blinded radiologist pairwise preference on terminology accuracy, readability, overall quality and authenticity of LLM-generated (DeepSeek-V3.2) versus human-edited Japanese translations
links.effect: Radiologist 1 rated terminology as equivalent in 59% of cases and favored the LLM translation for readability (51%) and overall quality (51%). Radiologist 2 rated readability as equivalent in 75% of cases and favored the human-edited translation for overall quality (40% vs 21%).
links.tradeoff: The two radiologists differed substantially (poor inter-rater agreement), so the preference for LLM translation was not consistent across raters.
links.quote: Radiologist 1 rated terminology as equivalent in 59% of cases and favored the LLM translation for readability (51%) and overall quality (51%).

design_hint: expert radiologist review versus LLM-as-a-judge evaluation of translations
